# Beiz Data & Accounting

> Finance workflows connected, reconciled and tested in the tools you already use. Led by an Australian Chartered Accountant. Canberra, working Australia-wide.

Beiz Data & Accounting Pty Ltd (ABN 53 691 755 496) fixes one recurring month-end workflow at a time where a business's systems and its ledger disagree: job systems, timesheets, payroll and bank data against Xero, MYOB or an ERP. The lead offer is a free 20-minute fit conversation, then a system-to-ledger exception review ($1,500–$2,500 AUD) and, where justified, a system-to-ledger exception sprint ($4,000–$8,000 AUD) built in the client's existing tools with written acceptance tests, documentation and handover. Maintenance is quoted only after the workload is measured. Every deliverable is reviewed by a Chartered Accountant before handover; nothing is paid or sent without a person. Principal: Purav Mehta, Chartered Accountant (CA ANZ) with a Certificate of Public Practice, GAICD. Not registered for GST; prices are AUD with no GST added.

Beiz does not provide tax returns, BAS or GST lodgements, tax or BAS agent services, statutory audit or assurance, legal advice or financial product advice.

# Full detail

## What Beiz does
Beiz Data & Accounting sets up AI agents for the routine finance and admin work in your business: bills, cash, reconciliations and client checks. Each agent is tested on your past records first, and anything it isn't sure about waits for a person.

Led by a Chartered Accountant, a member of Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand with a Certificate of Public Practice, and GAICD. Canberra, working Australia-wide.

## Is Beiz a fit?
- Who it's for: Outsourced bookkeeping and finance firms of around 5 to 25 staff, and Australian businesses and finance teams with one month-end job that keeps getting stuck.
- Hard limits: Works only in the systems you approve. Tested on your past records against acceptance tests agreed in writing. Runs beside your team before anything goes live. Nothing is paid or sent without a person. Every decision logged in your own accounts.
- Who reviews: An Australian Chartered Accountant (Certificate of Public Practice, GAICD) scopes the work and reviews every deliverable before handover. An agent never signs anything off.
- What we won't do: Tax returns, BAS or GST lodgements, tax or BAS agent services, statutory audit or assurance, legal advice, financial product advice, or payments released without a person.

## Where it helps
- Bills: today, evenings spent copying between emailed PDFs, bank feeds and your accounting software, and receipt apps reusing last month's account code. With a Beiz agent: Matched to the supplier and order. Duplicates, split bills and changed bank details held for you.
- Cash: today, the bank balance today and a guess about next month. With a Beiz agent: A 13-week cash view that refreshes from your weekly exports and ties back to the ledger.
- Reconciliations: today, month-end spent copying between your accounting software and spreadsheets. With a Beiz agent: Accounts matched on a schedule, with the exceptions listed for a person to clear.
- Client checks: today, new-client checks done from memory or an old checklist. With a Beiz agent: Each new client checked against your written procedure, with gaps flagged before work starts.

## Services

One month-end job where your systems and your ledger disagree, fixed in the tools you already own.

- Exception sprint ($4,000–$8,000): One agreed workflow built in your existing tools, with written acceptance tests, documentation and handover. $4,000–$8,000.
- Maintenance (Quoted): Limited monitoring and updates, quoted once the real workload is measured. Never open-ended.

Quoted in writing unless a price is shown.

- AI workflows & automation (From $8,500): We check what Xero, MYOB or your existing software already does first, then build only the gaps, tested and handed over. From $8,500.
- Automation acceptance testing (Quoted): Test cases from your own records, including duplicates, missing rows and changed file formats, before a workflow or agent goes live.

- Finance continuity (Quoted): Keep paying and reconciling when Microsoft or your ledger is down.
- Kits ($190–$290): A 13-week cash forecast ($290) and a supplier bank-change control kit ($190).

## Terms
- Credit: Where the proposal says so, the exception review fee is credited once against the exception sprint if you accept the sprint proposal and pay the deposit within 60 days of the diagnostic. It isn't redeemable for cash and doesn't apply to maintenance.
- Monthly operations: Covers up to two agreed agents or one model: a monthly control review, a log sample, a test re-run and up to two hours of fixes in total. More is quoted. Requests are acknowledged within two business days. It isn't round-the-clock monitoring or an emergency service.
- Cash model: You drop in fresh exports weekly and the model refreshes. Beiz builds it, ties actuals to the ledger, documents the assumptions and hands it over. Beiz reviews the forecast only where the support agreement sets out how often and what.
- Proposals: Every proposal has a fixed fee, a timeline and a definition of done, and arrives within three business days.

## How a build runs
- Write or talk: You describe the problem. A written reply by the next business day; calls are 20 minutes, early morning or after 5pm.
- Fixed proposal: Within three business days: a fixed fee, a timeline and a definition of done.
- Build and test: Built in your own systems and replayed on a period of your past records agreed in the proposal. You get a one-page test report: how many rows it matched, held and stopped, and every case where it disagreed with what your team actually did, measured against the acceptance tests agreed in writing.
- Run beside your team: The new workflow runs alongside the current one for an agreed period. Its output is compared with your team's before anything goes live.
- Hand over: Documentation, the decision log in your own accounts, and a review with you at day 30. The rules, scripts and procedure files are yours to keep, so you aren't tied to Beiz to keep it running.

## Rules first, AI for the exceptions
- Rules first: Fixed rules do the routine checking: matching amounts, dates, suppliers and invoice numbers. They behave the same way every time and cost nothing to run.
- AI for the exceptions: AI only looks at what the rules can't settle, like a supplier invoice laid out in an unusual way. It hands back a structured answer for the rules to check again.
- Figures from PDFs: PDF tables are positions on a page, not a spreadsheet, which is why general AI tools often misread them. Tables are read separately from the text, and every figure keeps a link to its document, page and line before it's checked against your ledger.
- A person decides: Anything held, unusual or over your limit goes to a named person, and a hold always wins: nothing further down the line can release it. Every run is kept in a history your staff can read, step by step.

## Every build includes
- A written scope: which inputs are supported, which rules you approve, what a complete output looks like and who reviews exceptions
- A test report from replaying your past records, measured against a pass mark agreed in writing
- A run beside your team before live
- A decision log kept in your own accounts
- A monthly spending cap and an off switch for anything that calls an AI model
- Nothing paid or sent without a person
- A day-30 review
- An operating folder you keep: business context, procedures, the rules and scripts, as plain files

## How a bill gets in
- Sort it first: Each attachment is sorted before anything is read: invoice, receipt, remittance advice or statement. A remittance advice never gets entered as a bill, and tiny images from email signatures are dropped before they cost anything.
- Check for doubles: Before a bill is added, it's looked up by supplier, ABN, invoice number and total. A forwarded copy or an "updated" invoice is held instead of entered twice.
- One record at a time: Rules handle each bill on its own, so a long export can't be skimmed. Only the bills the rules can't settle go to AI, which hands back a structured answer the rules check again.
- Don't trust the last code: Receipt apps often reuse last month's account code even when the invoice has changed. The agent checks the coding against the invoice itself and holds anything that doesn't match.

## Control status
- Planned: Written down: what the control checks, who owns it and what happens when it fails.
- Built: Running in your systems, but its decisions don't count yet.
- Tested beside your team: Run on your past records against the acceptance tests, then alongside your staff, with every difference explained.
- Reviewed and live: A named person at your business accepts the test results, and a Chartered Accountant at Beiz has reviewed the work. Only then does it run live within its limits.

## Stop conditions (work stops and waits for a person)
- A supplier's bank details change
- An ABN is missing or doesn't match the supplier's earlier bills
- An invoice number repeats, or an "updated" invoice arrives for one already paid
- A bill is over your approval limit, or several bills look split to stay under it
- The monthly spending cap is reached, or a person presses the off switch

## Each service in brief
### System-to-ledger exception review (https://beiz.com.au/cash-data-check/)
- For owners and finance leads who bill time or fixed fees and suspect work or money is slipping.
- Two weeks, from your exports: bills, invoices and timesheets checked against each other, every finding traced to its record.
- No logins to your ledger, no tax or BAS advice. The fee is credited if you go ahead with a build.
### AI workflows & automation (https://beiz.com.au/services/automation/)
- For teams doing the same matching, chasing and checking every week.
- One workflow automated with fixed rules for the routine records and AI only for the exceptions, then tested and handed over.
- Runs in your own accounts, with a run history your staff can read and a person approving anything that matters.
### Compliance controls sprint (https://beiz.com.au/compliance-sprint/)
- For businesses facing one obligation now: AI use, AML/CTF tranche 2 or the Privacy Act automated-decision rules.
- Two weeks: what's in scope, who owns each step, where a person must approve, and a plan for the first controlled workflow.
- General information, not legal advice. Your adviser or lawyer keeps the legal wording.
### AML/CTF for accounting firms (https://beiz.com.au/aml-ctf-accounting-firms/)
- For accounting firms working out whether the services they provide bring them under AUSTRAC's AML/CTF rules.
- Agents collect, check and file the routine client checks. Your compliance officer decides every risk rating and every report.
- Sized for small firms. General information, not legal advice.

## Decision log fields
- Record: The bill: supplier, invoice number, date and amount.
- Check: The rule that ran, in plain words.
- Finding: What the check saw in the records, with the records it compared.
- Status: ok, held for a person, or stopped before payment.
- Who decides: The named person who clears it, and what they do next. Their decision is logged with their name and the time.

## Free bill check
Catch an updated invoice about to be paid twice, or a supplier whose bank details just changed, before the payment run. Drop in a bills export from Xero, MYOB or QuickBooks, or any spreadsheet saved as CSV. Eight checks run on this device in a few seconds. Your file isn't uploaded, stored or sent to us.
- Possible duplicate bills: same supplier, same amount, within 14 days, including an updated invoice sent after the original
- The same invoice number used twice by one supplier
- A supplier's bank details changing
- Bills that look split to stay under your approval limit
- Bills just under your approval limit
- A large first bill from a supplier first seen in your file
- Payments made on a weekend
- ABNs missing or failing the check-digit test

Q: Is my bills file uploaded anywhere?
A: No. The check runs in your browser on your own device. Your file isn't uploaded, stored or sent to Beiz.
Q: Which accounting software does it work with?
A: Any bills or payables export saved as CSV, including from Xero, MYOB and QuickBooks. It needs a supplier, an amount and a date; invoice numbers, payment dates, bank details and ABNs make it sharper.
Q: Why not paste my bills into ChatGPT?
A: You can, but a chat assistant reads a file loosely and can skip or misread rows in a long export. This check runs the same fixed rules on every row, shows each flag with the records behind it, and your file never leaves your device. Check your own obligations before putting supplier bank details or client information into any online AI tool.
Q: Is this an audit?
A: No. It's eight quick checks. A flag is a prompt for a person to look, and many flags will have an innocent explanation.
Q: What does it cost?
A: Nothing. The paid two-week cash and data check goes further, from your full exports, at a fixed fee agreed in writing.

It's eight quick checks, not an audit. It can't see your bank, your emails or the bills you never entered, and it doesn't tell you whether anyone did anything wrong. It's general information, not tax, legal or accounting advice, and you decide what to do with any flag. Xero, MYOB and QuickBooks are named only to describe file formats; Beiz isn't affiliated with them.

## What Beiz does not do
Beiz doesn't do tax returns, BAS or GST lodgements, tax or BAS agent services, statutory audit or assurance, legal advice or financial product advice, and never releases payments without a person. Your tax agent keeps that work.
